title: para vs por, razón, el día, todos los días, trabajar

cards.title: Gracias por venir
cards.body: 'Thanks for coming.' This phrase is a hook: Spanish has two words for 'for'.

cards.title: para = for (someone)
cards.body: When you can't recall a word, find it through a phrase you know (esta noche → este).

cards.title: por = because of
cards.body: Por qué = 'because of what' (why); porque = because. Razón (reason) is feminine.

examples.en: For this reason, I don't want to go.
examples.es: Por esta razón, no quiero ir.

cards.title: para ti vs por ti
cards.body: An ashtray bought for a smoker friend: lo he comprado para ti means it's theirs to take home; por ti means you bought it because of them.

examples.en: I'm buying it because of you.

cards.title: por + period of time; el día
cards.body: Día (from an old root meaning light, like 'deity' and 'Jupiter') is masculine despite the -a. Every day = 'all the days'. Tres = three.

cards.title: Hook for 'would': me gustaría
cards.body: Pull the -ía ending from me gustaría. Trabajar = to work (j = throaty h).

examples.en: I'd stay for three days, but I have to work.
examples.es: Me quedaría por tres días, pero tengo que trabajar.
